> But the strangest thing I've noticed is that no one really knows how to be at gatherings any longer.
>
> There's no norm here of, like, brining a bottle of wine when you come to someone's house. There's no norm of circulating with strangers. There's definitely no norm of dressing well. Folks don't even really seem to know why they would want to get together.

Biao Xiang’s concept of [The Nearby](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355953022_The_nearby_A_scope_of_seeing) is interesting here. To the extent this thesis is true it’s global not American, and an interesting twist in the more America-centric Putnam thesis in Bowling Alone.
content_html:
But the strangest thing I've noticed is that no one really knows how to be at gatherings any longer.

There's no norm here of, like, brining a bottle of wine when you come to someone's house. There's no norm of circulating with strangers. There's definitely no norm of dressing well. Folks don't even really seem to know why they would want to get together.

Biao Xiang’s concept of The Nearby is interesting here. To the extent this thesis is true it’s global not American, and an interesting twist in the more America-centric Putnam thesis in Bowling Alone.
